# 0010: SVG bar charts embedded in README, generated by docs/benchcharts

## Status

Accepted

## Context

README.md's benchmark numbers were plain fenced-code-block text. Wanted a
visual bar-chart representation in addition to (not instead of) the raw
numbers, without adding a runtime or build dependency on an external
charting library, and without embedding non-reviewable binary image blobs.

## Decision

Added `docs/benchcharts/main.go` — a standalone `package main` program (not
part of the `goache` library, built freely by `go build ./...` since it's a
valid package but never imported by anything) that generates plain SVG bar
charts as text, with benchmark data hardcoded to match the numbers already
documented in README.md. Output goes to `docs/img/*.svg`, embedded in
README.md via standard markdown `![alt](path)` image syntax (renders
natively on GitHub, no JS/external service required).

Charts generated: `core-ops.svg` (Set/SetMany/Get/GetMiss/ParallelGetSet/
ParallelGet), `capacity-hint.svg` (`WithCapacity` before/after), `compare-
set.svg` and `compare-parallel-get.svg` (goache vs go-cache/freecache/
ristretto, goache's bar highlighted in a distinct color).

Regenerate via `make charts` after updating benchmark numbers elsewhere in
README.md — the data in `docs/benchcharts/main.go` is hand-kept in sync,
not automatically extracted from benchmark output.

## Why this approach

- **Plain SVG text, self-authored**: reviewable in a diff like any other
  text file (no binary blob, no opaque PNG). No dependency on gnuplot,
  matplotlib, D3, or any charting library — just `fmt.Fprintf` building SVG
  markup directly, keeping the "goache itself must stay dependency-free"
  principle intact even for tooling.
- **Static, committed images** rather than generating charts at README-view
  time: GitHub markdown rendering can't execute code, so charts must exist
  as files ahead of time regardless of approach.
- **Hand-synced data, not extracted from `go test -bench` output**: the
  README numbers are themselves hand-curated (specific runs picked as
  representative, with system-noise outliers already filtered out by
  hand — see e.g. the false-start 44ns reading during
  [0004](0004-shard-storage-pointer-slice.md)'s investigation). Auto-
  extracting from raw benchmark output would either re-introduce that noise
  or require the same manual curation step anyway, just moved.

## Consequences

- Two places to update when benchmark numbers change: the fenced code block
  text in README.md, and the matching `bar{}` entries in
  `docs/benchcharts/main.go`, then `make charts` to regenerate the SVGs.
  Easy to let these drift — if a future change updates one and not the
  other, fix both before considering the change done.
- No new runtime or module dependency; `docs/benchcharts` uses only the Go
  standard library.
